headline: Majors hold above the 200-day while momentum maxes out; whales dumping into exchanges this week, but the flow regime reversed hard from early August.
paragraphs: All seven majors sit above their 200-day moving averages, and all seven have MACD above signal line, which is the kind of unanimous statement that should make you pay attention to what it does NOT say: none of them have triggered a golden cross yet. That means the 50-day has not reclaimed the 200-day, so the longer-term trend is still down even as price has climbed. This is a rally inside a downtrend, not a trend reversal. Bitcoin at 79,093 is still 36.6% below its 12-month high of 124,740. Ethereum sits 47.5% below its peak. Solana and Doge are each 61-68% underwater from their recent tops. The regime is: price recovered sharply off the lows, momentum is hot, but the ceiling from earlier in the year remains in place.

Momentum readings are at extremes across the board. Bitcoin RSI sits at 82.3, Ethereum at 80.2, Solana at 84.3, BNB at 84.6. These are overbought levels by the standard textbook definition, yet price keeps moving. A divergence between oscillator and trend is normally a warning flag, but here the divergence is between oscillator and the longer timeframe: the 14-period is screaming fast, the 200-day is still pointing down. The seven-day and 30-day price changes tell the story of the move: Bitcoin up 25.55% in the week and 24.07% in the month, Ethereum up 33.43% and 38.98%, XRP up 49.91% in the week (though it fell 1.53% today), and even Doge, which dropped 2.23% today, is up 30.42% over the week. This is a crowd that has arrived at the party late and is bidding hard.

Perp funding at 11% annualized (0.01% per 8 hours across the board) is elevated but not stratospheric by historical crypto standards. Open interest is substantial: 2.33 billion in BTC, 1.46 billion in ETH, 271 million in SOL. The long-to-short ratio tells a clearer story. Bitcoin is 1.08 longs per short, which is mild. Ethereum is 1.12. But SOL is 1.99, XRP is 2.12, and Doge sits at 3.48 longs for every short. The micro caps are crowded with leverage on one side. Liquidations over the past four to 24 hours show shorts getting flushed more than longs: in BTC, shorts liquidated for 11.6 million against 6.3 million in longs. In SOL over the last day, longs gave up 4.56 million while shorts gave up only 1.41 million. The directional squeeze is asymmetric, favoring short hunters.

Whale flows show a critical reversal that is still unfolding. Over the last 48 hours, 63.5 million moved off exchanges, led by 88.4 million in Bitcoin exiting Kraken. That sounds accumulative, the classic sign of hands moving to cold storage. But zoom to the weekly view: the week of August 3 saw 1.14 billion move off exchanges. The three weeks since have reversed that completely: August 10 saw 288 million move onto exchanges, August 17 saw 277 million move onto, and this week ending August 24 has seen 1.091 billion move onto exchanges. That is a flood. Meanwhile, stablecoin float sits at 308.6 billion, unchanged over the last 30 days (plus 0.01%), so dry powder is not accumulating even as coins move onto exchange wallets. The picture: spot ETF inflows are persistent (five straight sessions positive, 1.918 billion over the last five sessions for Bitcoin, 693 million for Ethereum, cumulative 53.8 billion for BTC year to date) but whales are pressing coins onto trading platforms, which is pressure, not support.

The Fear and Greed gauge is at 73, labeled Greed, and over the last 30 days has ranged from 25 to 73. This is a crowd that went from extreme fear to maximum greed in a month. Total market cap is 2.688 trillion (up slightly today, but down 0.34% in the last 24 hours despite Bitcoin and Ethereum both higher), and Bitcoin dominance sits at 59%, which is stable but not extreme. The top movers outside the majors show fragmentation: AERO up 12.22%, PENGU up 11.96%, INJ up 10.3%, but TRUMP down 14.04% and ZRO down 9.96%. This is not a market-wide impulse; it is selected retail rotation into and out of positions.

Watch for three things: First, whether Bitcoin and Ethereum trigger a golden cross in the sessions ahead (a 50-day reclaim of the 200-day would confirm the reversal narrative that momentum is now hinting at). Second, whether the weekly whale flow reverses again next week, as the last four weeks show extreme swings between accumulation and distribution. Third, whether the long-to-short ratio in the alts (especially SOL and Doge) begins to compress: if leverage unwinds from overbought, even with positive momentum, the exit door gets crowded. The tape today says price is elevated, positioning is hot, and large holders are liquidating into retail bids. That framing is not bullish or bearish by itself; it is just what the money is doing.
